title: vocabularies.terms
description: A whole level's terms as (code, label) pairs — the BROWSE read behind resolver.terms(), which stapel-categories expands a category's children from. This object validates the request payload; the response shape ({terms, truncated, extras?}) is documented in $defs.Terms, and an unknown vocabulary or level answers null. Not vocabularies.children with a bigger number: children is a PAGE for a caller reasoning about a set (MAX_PAGE_SIZE, a typeahead's size, parent named as a {level, code} pair); this is the whole level for a caller RENDERING it (TERMS_LIMIT, parent given as the bare code it descended through).

level.description: Level to list. An unknown level answers null, never an empty list.

parent.description: A term CODE at the level ABOVE this one — the code a browser descended through, which is all it holds. When given, only the terms this parent scopes are listed. A parent that names no term scopes NOTHING and answers an empty list, never the whole level; so does any parent at all on a root level.

limit.description: How many terms to answer, clamped to 1..TERMS_LIMIT (default TERMS_LIMIT).

terms.description: The terms as [code, label] pairs, in the level's own order (popular band first, then the curated rank, then the label).

extras.description: The source catalogue's own per-term attributes, keyed by term code — {"chernyy": {"hue": "#1a1a1a"}} on a colour level, so a facet can draw a swatch (stapel-vocabularies >= 0.4.0). Only the terms that carry any appear, and the key is absent entirely when none do. Deliberately NOT a third element of each `terms` row: a 0.3.0 reader unpacks those rows as pairs (`for code, label in rows` in CommResolver.terms; a [:2] slice in stapel-categories' branching), so a wider row would make a 0.4.0 catalogue service break every 0.3.0 caller in the fleet, while a key an old reader does not know is simply not read. A caller that wants the bag alongside the labels uses resolver.terms_with_extra(), which zips the two here.

truncated.description: Whether the level holds more terms than came back. Not a cursor and deliberately not paginated: it is the browse read admitting that a level over TERMS_LIMIT should not be a browse level at all — put a coarser level above it and expand the category by that.
